review_2026_09_18.independent_remeasurement: Every CAD number below was recomputed from assets/meshes/reference/matrice4-M4T_v2.step in a separate isolated copy of HEAD 4254c4b2 (live sha256 src/drones.py 9f35d2a6…, src/drone_cad.py 4f706fc7…, benchmark/elevation_sweep_md.py c6403bd7…), using cad_tris.npz (12:40 pass) and, as a second independent extraction, cad_edges.npz (12:07 pass). The two passes give the bounding box as 328.265 x 387.385 x 151.520 mm and 328.278 x 387.501 x 151.524 mm — agreeing to 0.013 / 0.116 / 0.004 mm, and the edge pass matches DJI's published width 387.5 mm to 0.001 mm.
review_2026_09_18.solid_id_caveat: ⚠ The solid ids used throughout this file (49, 56-58, 92, 95/96, 98, 103, 105, 109, 116, 118, 119, 120, 122/26, 123, 124) are gmsh volume tags of ONE triangulation pass (scratch mesh_0917/matrice4e/cad_tris.npz), which is scratch and will disappear. The repository's own August comments on the same CAD use a DIFFERENT numbering — src/drone_cad.py calls the battery bay solid 117, the bells 104/94 and the arms 107/97/86/91. The DIMENSIONS agree exactly (bay front face +70.10 and floor -6.14 in both), only the tags differ. Anyone re-checking must re-derive the tags, not assume them.

corrections.M4E-4a heading 67.04 deg: ⚠ METHOD-DEPENDENT BY MORE THAN THE FILE SUGGESTS. Recomputed on solid 98: the AREA-weighted principal axis gives 67.58 deg and the straight-line fit through the mid-span section centres gives 66.79 deg, against this file's 67.04 / 65.75. The stated tolerance is +/-1.0 deg, i.e. only about twice the spread between two reasonable estimators. All the estimates stay inside the plan's 66-68 deg band, so the target holds, but the number should be quoted as 67 +/- 0.5 (method), not 67.04.
corrections.M4E-4b x at |y| = 47.08: recomputed as 85.50 mm (this file says the CAD gives 82.7). Both are inside the plan's 85 +/- 5; the difference is the same estimator spread as M4E-4a.
corrections.M4E-4c bow 'collinear to 0.6 mm': ⚠ OPTIMISTIC. Recomputed: the mid-span (t -63.5..+31.5) section centres of solid 98 deviate from their best-fit straight line by up to 1.13 mm, not 0.6 mm. The built arm's own bow is 0.0 by construction, so the target still holds; only the description of the CAD is wrong.
corrections.M4E-6d 'brings that number to 0.000 %': ⚠ NOT EXACTLY ZERO. The repository's own mesh_check.check_prop_bell_solid on the built revision-1 drone still finds 8 propeller triangles, 0.15 mm2, inside the motor solid (0.0003 % of the propeller area) at the 1.5 mm standoff. That is far inside the 0.1 % budget and is not a defect, but '0.000 %' should read '<= 0.0004 %'.

DECLARED MESH-VALIDITY GAP: the 1.5 mm standoff is not a physical claim. The P6 blade's root loft hangs up to 1.93 mm below the hub underside inside r <= 13.5 mm, so seating the hub flat on the flat-topped CAD adapter puts 304 blade triangles (0.526 % of the propeller area) inside the motor solid against mesh_check's 0.1 % budget. 1.5 mm is the smallest 0.5 mm step that brings that number to 0.000 %. targets.component: front and rear arm shafts (P4 straight_arm section law)
targets.what: DEFECT FOUND BY THE REVIEW 2026-09-18, FIXED 2026-09-18: the arm section was interpolated LINEARLY from root to motor pad, so the pad flare was smeared over the whole arm and the mid-span shaft came out roughly twice the CAD width
targets.source: true plane sections of CAD front-arm solid 98 and of the built body group, taken normal to the CAD arm axis every 7.5 mm; plan-view areas rasterised at 1 mm in the window |y| > 55 mm, r < 205 mm
targets.note: The CAD shaft is nearly constant at 11.8-12.7 mm from t=-60 to t=+30 and only then flares to 27.5 mm over the last ~22 mm. Revision 1 is +10.7 mm at mid-span and +13.6 mm at t=+30 (2.15x the CAD). The one-sided CAD->ours distance cannot see this (every CAD point still finds a near neighbour on the larger arm) and the reverse distance, 5.87 mm p90, sits just under the lambda/10 limit of 8.6 mm, so the frozen acceptance passes it. The plan-view area is the statistic that shows it: the arm shafts project 11,585 mm2 against the CAD's 6,235 and revision 0's 7,418 — i.e. revision 1 ADDS about 4,200 mm2 of plastic area at exactly the nadir and zenith aspects where removing the 5,572 mm2 metal plate (M4E-1) is the headline change. P4's API is frozen and interpolates linearly, so the fix is to build each arm as two straight_arm segments — a constant 12.2 mm shaft to t=+30, then the flare to the 27.6 mm pad. NOT DONE HERE: it is a geometry change and belongs to the builder.
targets.fix: Each arm is now two P4 `straight_arm` segments on one axis (P4's API unchanged): a shaft from the root to d = 20 mm with the CAD's near-constant section, then the flare to the motor pad. Measured effect: the arm-shaft plan-view area (the review's own statistic, window |y| > 55 mm and r < 205 mm) goes 11,585 -> 6,725 mm2 against the CAD's 6,235 and revision 0's 7,418 — revision 1 is now CLOSER to the CAD than revision 0 is (+490 vs +1,183 mm2), which is the rule plan C.4 states. Both one-sided distances improved as well: CAD->ours front_arms p90 3.345 -> 2.541 mm, ours->CAD front_arms p90 5.871 -> 3.192 mm, ours->CAD rear_arms p99 7.960 -> 3.414 mm (that row was one of the 13 failures). Top-view silhouette IoU against the CAD 0.853 -> 0.927.

targets.what: which propeller the campaign aircraft flies
targets.source: user decision 2026-09-18. DJI's Matrice 4 Series spec page lists both 1157F (standard) and 1154F (low-noise); the User Manual v1.2 accessory and spare-parts tables on p.103 list ONLY 1154F (27.4 x 13.7 cm), which is why the build and the review both reported 1154F as the manual's answer. The DJI part-number rule 11-5-7-F reads as 10.8 in diameter and 5.7 in pitch.
targets.note: No geometry changes. drones.py PROP_LAW_0816 already names 1157F; prop_dia_mm stays 274 mm, prop_blades 2, and plan B.0 forbids changing either in a revision. Recorded so that the earlier 'the manual lists only 1154F' finding is not read as a correction to the code.
